section.title: Stash
section.p: Use: Opens a drop-down menu for creating a stash or listing existing stashes.

Details: A stash saves local changes outside the normal commit history so you can return the working copy to a clean state. The saved changes can be applied later to the same repository. This is useful before switching branches, pulling changes, or running an operation that requires no local changes.
Best Practice: Use a stash when you need a clean working copy and want to reapply the changes later.
Accessible From: Git Staging view toolbar.

section.title: Stash Changes
section.p: Use: Creates a new stash from the changed files in the working copy.

Details: The action stores the current local changes in the stash list and removes them from the working copy. Git keeps the stash separate from branch history, so it is not shared with other users and is not pushed to the remote repository.
Scope: Changed files in the current working copy.

ul.li: Stash drop-down menu in the Git Staging view toolbar.

section.title: List Stashes
section.p: Use: Opens a dialog box that lists existing stashes for the current repository.

Details: The stash list shows saved work that is not part of the current branch history. From this list, you can apply a stash to restore its changes in the working copy or remove a stash that is no longer needed.

ul.li: Stash drop-down menu in the Git Staging view toolbar.

section.title: Apply Stash
section.p: Use: Applies a selected stash to the current working copy.

Details: Applying a stash restores the saved changes on top of the current working copy state. The operation can create conflicts if the same files changed after the stash was created. Applying a stash does not create a commit.
Scope: Selected stash and current working copy.
Accessible From: Stash list dialog box.

section.title: Remove Stash
section.p: Use: Deletes a selected stash from the stash list.

Details: Removing a stash deletes the saved changes from the local repository stash storage. The action does not affect commits or files that already exist in the working copy, but the removed stash cannot be applied later.
Caution: Remove a stash only when you no longer need the saved changes.
Accessible From: Stash list dialog box.

section.title: Submodule
section.p: Use: Opens a control where you can select a submodule to open and work with.

Details: A submodule is a separate Git repository recorded inside another repository. The parent repository stores a reference to a specific submodule commit. Use this control to switch the Git Client context to a submodule when you need to inspect or change its files.
Availability: Enabled when the repository contains submodules. When you clone a repository with submodules, the Git Client initializes and clones the submodules.

section.title: Open Submodule
section.p: Use: Opens the selected submodule so you can work with it as a repository.

Details: The Git Client uses the selected submodule as the active working copy. This lets you review, stage, commit, pull, and push changes inside the submodule repository instead of the parent repository.
Scope: Selected submodule.

ul.li: Open context menu action for a modified submodule in the Unstaged files area.
